mainTopic: When a קרבן's atonement begins, slaughtering a תודה for a friend's תודה, and רבא's rulings on a חטאת slaughtered with the wrong type or for the wrong person.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that a קרבן atones for sins done after it was set aside (הפרשה). The proof comes from the argument between רבי שמעון and the חכמים about redeeming leftover unblemished communal animals. A second proof, from רבי ירמיה's question about the two שעירי עצרת, is rejected: he may have been asking 'אם תימצי לומר'. Next, רבה and רב חסדא argue about a תודה slaughtered for the sake of a friend's תודה. רבה tries to prove from a ברייתא that it is כשרה, but the גמרא shows the ברייתא could be talking about the owner's own other תודה. Then רבא gives a set of rulings about a חטאת. Slaughtered for another חטאת, it is כשרה. Slaughtered for an עולה, it is פסולה. Slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת, or who seems to owe nothing, it is פסולה. Slaughtered for a person who owes only an עולה, it is כשרה. רבא also says a חטאת atones for missed positive מצוות, and the amud ends with the גמרא asking how that fits his ruling about the person who owes an עולה.

steps.title: End of the first proof: רבי שמעון and the חכמים on redeeming unblemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The proof finishes. According to רבי שמעון, leftover unblemished communal animals cannot be redeemed. According to the חכמים, they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, they are not redeemed while unblemished. According to the חכמים, they are redeemed even while unblemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source it is using as proof. Leftover communal animals can be redeemed while unblemished according to the חכמים, but not according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that בית דין makes a condition: animals that are not needed never become fully holy, so they can be redeemed unblemished. רבי שמעון rejects this, so for him the animals are holy right from הפרשה. That shows a קרבן's status, and its power to atone, can begin at הפרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: are redeemed (their holiness is moved onto money)
unblemished animals
the Sages (the majority opinion)

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Shimon,
they are not redeemed while unblemished,
according to the words of the Sages,
they are redeemed while unblemished!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרבן atones for a positive-מצוה violation done after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי שמעון and the חכמים about redeeming leftover unblemished communal animals.

steps.title: Second proof: רבי ירמיה's question about the two שעירי עצרת
steps.stepSummary: 'ועוד' introduces another proof. רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא what the second שעיר עצרת atones for. רבי זירא answered that it atones for impurity that happened between the two sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא about the goats of עצרת whose blood was collected in two cups. The blood of the first goat was sprinkled. What is the second goat brought for? He answered: for impurity that happened between the sprinkling of this one and that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source to help prove the same point. It quotes a question and answer here, and draws the actual proof from it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both goats were slaughtered together. Once the first one's blood is sprinkled, it seems nothing is left for the second to atone for. רבי זירא answers that the second goat atones for impurity that happened in the short gap between the two sprinklings, which is after its שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore (introduces an additional proof)
the goats brought as offerings on שבועות
cups (vessels for collecting blood)
was sprinkled (the blood on the מזבח)
happened, occurred

phrases.english: And furthermore,

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
The goats of Shavuot
whose blood one collected in two cups,
and the blood of the first one was sprinkled;
the second one, what is it brought for?
For impurity that happened
between [the sprinkling of] this one and that one.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, which makes clear the gap is between the two sprinklings.

phrases.english: (If the blood of the second was sprinkled,
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves them out.

phrases.english: what are they offered for?)

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent proof for the same claim.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרבן atones for a positive-מצוה violation done after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ירמיה's question to רבי זירא about the two שעירי עצרת.

steps.title: The inference: רבי ירמיה only doubted sins done after שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asked only about a violation after שחיטה. So he must have taken it as obvious that a קרבן atones for a violation after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He only had a question about a positive מצוה violated after שחיטה. But about a positive מצוה violated after הפרשה, he had no question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its proof from the question in the last step. רבי ירמיה wondered only about sins after שחיטה, so sins after הפרשה must have been clear to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic works by noticing what was not asked. If atonement for sins after הפרשה were also in doubt, רבי ירמיה would have asked about that first. His silence suggests he already accepted that a קרבן atones for them.

keyTerms.meaning: he only had a question about this much
a positive מצוה (here, a violation of one)
slaughtering the animal
designating (setting aside) the animal as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: There are two time points here. הפרשה (setting the animal aside) comes first, and שחיטה (slaughtering it) comes later. The question is whether atonement covers sins from each of those points onward.

phrases.english: He only had a question
about a positive מצוה violated after slaughtering,
but about a positive מצוה violated after designation
he had no question!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the question and answer quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרבן atones for a positive-מצוה violation done after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that רבי ירמיה asked only about violations after שחיטה.

steps.title: Rejection: maybe he was asking 'even if you say'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. רבי ירמיה may have been asking 'אם תימצי לומר': even if you grant that a קרבן atones for sins after הפרשה, does it also atone for sins after שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he was saying, 'If you will say...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי ירמיה. His question may have been built in layers, so he may have been unsure about sins after הפרשה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אם תימצי לומר' means: 'even if you answer the first question one way, I still ask the second.' So asking only about sins after שחיטה does not prove that sins after הפרשה were obvious to him. He may simply have skipped ahead to the harder case.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps
'if you will say', meaning even if you grant the first point
he was saying

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי ירמיה fails because his question may have been an 'אם תימצי לומר' question. That kind of question takes the first issue as granted only for argument's sake, without being sure of it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אם תימצי לומר' does not mean the asker agreed with the first point. It only means he was setting it aside for the moment to ask the next question.

phrases.english: Perhaps he was saying, "if you will say."
phrases.notes: He means: even if you grant that a קרבן atones for sins after it was set aside, what about sins after it was slaughtered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the second proof (from רבי ירמיה) is rejected. The first proof from רבי שמעון is not addressed here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumes that what was not asked must have been obvious. But the question may have been an 'אם תימצי לומר' question, which leaves the first issue unresolved.

steps.title: Dispute over a thanks offering slaughtered for another person's thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a תודה slaughtered for the sake of a friend's תודה is כשרה. רב חסדא rules that it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone slaughtered a תודה for the sake of his friend's תודה, רבה says it is כשרה and רב חסדא says it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a disagreement between two אמוראים about one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal really is a תודה, and it was slaughtered as a תודה. The only problem is that the person slaughtering it had in mind that it belongs to someone else. The question is whether that wrong owner-intent ruins it.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering
His friend's thanks offering
Fit, valid
Unfit, invalid

phrases.english: It was stated:
A thanks offering that one slaughtered for the sake of his friend's thanks offering
(is fit) –
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out this word in round brackets. It makes sense to leave it out, since the next lines are where they argue about whether it is fit.

phrases.english: Rabba says: it is fit,
Rav Chisda says: it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: תּוֹדָה שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם תּוֹדַת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the previous discussion of what a קרבן atones for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a תודה slaughtered for a friend's תודה is כשרה. רב חסדא: it is פסולה.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבה: it is still a תודה slaughtered as a תודה. רב חסדא: it must be slaughtered for the sake of the owner's own offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says it is כשרה because a תודה was slaughtered for the sake of a תודה. רב חסדא says it is פסולה because we need it to be slaughtered for the sake of the owner's own שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looks only at the type of offering. The type matched, so nothing went wrong. רב חסדא says the intent must match the owner too: having in mind someone else's offering counts as the wrong intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering. A תודה is a kind of שלמים.
His own
We require

phrases.english: Rabba says it is fit –
a thanks offering was slaughtered for the sake of a thanks offering.
Rav Chisda says it is unfit –
we require that it be slaughtered for the sake of his own peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר כְּשֵׁרָה – תּוֹדָה לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה נִשְׁחֲטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind each opinion from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבה, matching the type of offering is enough. For רב חסדא, the intent must also match the true owner.

steps.title: רבה brings a ברייתא about thanks and peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבה cites אבא חנין in the name of רבי אליעזר. A תודה slaughtered as a שלמים is כשרה, but a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is פסולה, because a תודה is called a שלמים but not the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: How do I know this? From a ברייתא on the פסוק "and the meat of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering." אבא חנין said in the name of רבי אליעזר that it teaches this: a תודה slaughtered as a שלמים is כשרה, and a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is פסולה. The difference is that the תורה calls a תודה a שלמים, but never calls a שלמים a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts bringing a source to back up his view. The ברייתא he quotes is his raw material, and the next step shows how he uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the words "תודה" and "שלמים," which shows that a תודה counts as a kind of שלמים. So slaughtering a תודה as a שלמים is not really the wrong intent. Slaughtering a plain שלמים as a תודה is the wrong intent, so it is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? Introduces a speaker's own proof.
Difference
Is called

phrases.english: Rabba said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught in a baraita: "And the meat of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering
on the day that he offers his sacrifice, etc." –

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנִין אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: Abba Chanin said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
It comes to teach:
A thanks offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering is fit,
a peace offering that was slaughtered for the sake of a thanks offering is unfit.
And what is the difference between this and that?
A thanks offering is called a peace offering,
phrases.notes: That's right in the פסוק: "his thanksgiving peace offering."

phrases.english: but a peace offering is not called a thanks offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה starts proving his opinion from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that a תודה slaughtered for a friend's תודה is כשרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: אבא חנין in the name of רבי אליעזר on ויקרא 7:15

steps.title: רבה's inference: a thanks offering for a thanks offering is fit
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, רבה infers that a תודה slaughtered as a תודה is כשרה. He argues that this must mean another person's תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is פסולה. That implies a תודה slaughtered as a תודה is כשרה. What case is that? Isn't it talking about a friend's תודה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his proof. He pulls out what the ברייתא implies and argues it supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the problem is a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה. That suggests that a תודה slaughtered as a תודה is fine. A תודה slaughtered as its own תודה is too obvious to need teaching. So רבה argues the implied case must be a תודה slaughtered as someone else's תודה, which is exactly his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But this implies (introduces an inference)
What, is it not...? (pushing for a specific reading)
Of his friend, another person's

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read "תודה לשם תודה" as the normal case of slaughtering your own offering properly. רבה's whole point is that it must mean slaughtering it as someone else's תודה.

phrases.english: A peace offering for the sake of a thanks offering is unfit,
which implies a thanks offering for the sake of a thanks offering is fit;
what is this? Is it not his friend's?
phrases.notes: He means: isn't it a תודה slaughtered as his friend's תודה? That's exactly the case רבה and רב חסדא argue about.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלָמִים לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה – פְּסוּלָה, הָא תּוֹדָה לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה – כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 7 to complete רבה's proof.
steps.raayaObject: A תודה slaughtered for a friend's תודה is כשרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied ruling in the ברייתא of אבא חנין that a תודה slaughtered as a תודה is כשרה

steps.title: No, it means his own other thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבה's reading. The ברייתא's 'תודה slaughtered as a תודה' could mean the owner's own other תודה, not a friend's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבה's proof from Step 8. The case of a תודה slaughtered as a תודה might refer to a second תודה that belongs to the same owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה argued that 'a תודה slaughtered as a תודה' must mean another person's תודה, since slaughtering a תודה as itself is obvious. The answer is that it can mean a different תודה of the same owner, brought for a different rescue. So the ברייתא says nothing about a friend's תודה, and רב חסדא can still hold that it is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: No. It opens a rejection.
His own. Here it means another offering belonging to the same owner.

steps.confusionAlert: 'His own' here does not mean the very same animal. It means a different תודה that the same owner set aside, for example to thank ה׳ for a different rescue.

phrases.english: No, it means his own.
phrases.notes: He means the owner's own other thanks offering, not his friend's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's reading of the ברייתא in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבה's ruling itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה assumed the case had to mean a friend's תודה. It can just as well mean the owner's own second תודה.

steps.title: Then the teaching should have used the friend's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. If a friend's תודה would be פסולה, the ברייתא should have taught that case, and the case of a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה would follow all the more so.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a friend's thanks offering, what is the law? Is it unfit? If so, instead of teaching 'a peace offering for the sake of a thanks offering is unfit,' let it teach 'a thanks offering for the sake of a thanks offering,' and all the more so a peace offering for the sake of a thanks offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the rejection in Step 9. It asks why the ברייתא chose its example if a friend's תודה would also be פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a תודה slaughtered for a friend's תודה is פסולה, that is the bigger news, because the two offerings are the same type. A שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is a different type, so it would obviously be פסולה too (a כל שכן). Since the ברייתא chose the weaker case, it seems the friend's case is actually כשרה, which supports רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Of his friend, meaning another person's offering.
Instead of teaching.
Let it teach. This suggests a better way to word the teaching.
All the more so. It shows the second case follows easily from the first.

phrases.english: But a friend's, what is the law? Is it unfit?
Instead of teaching 'a peace offering for the sake of a thanks offering is unfit,'
let it teach 'a thanks offering for the sake of a thanks offering,'
phrases.notes: Read this as a thanks offering slaughtered for a friend's thanks offering, and so unfit.

phrases.english: and all the more so a peace offering for the sake of a thanks offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 9 by asking why the ברייתא chose its example.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a friend's תודה could be פסולה, as רב חסדא holds, while the ברייתא speaks only of the owner's own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching should state the bigger news. If a friend's תודה were פסולה, that case would teach more, and the שלמים case would follow from it as a כל שכן.

steps.title: The peace offering case was needed for its own reason
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed the case of a שלמים slaughtered for the owner's own תודה. Otherwise one might think that since a תודה is called a שלמים, a שלמים is also called a תודה and would be כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A peace offering for the sake of his own thanks offering was needed. It would enter your mind to say: since a thanks offering is called a 'peace offering,' a peace offering is also called a 'thanks offering,' so when one slaughters it for the sake of a thanks offering it should be fit. So it teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא picked the שלמים case on purpose, to block a mistaken idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a friend's תודה is פסולה, the שלמים case still teaches something new. The תורה calls a תודה a 'שלמים', so we might have thought the names work both ways and that a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is fine. The ברייתא teaches that the names do not work both ways, so it gives no proof about a friend's תודה, and רב חסדא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary. The case had to be taught.
It would enter your mind to say. It introduces a mistaken first thought.
Is called. It refers to an offering's name in the Torah.
It teaches us. It introduces the new lesson that corrects the mistaken thought.

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's proof from the ברייתא does not work. 'A תודה for a תודה' may mean the owner's own, and the שלמים case was taught to show that the names only work one way. The dispute between רבה and רב חסדא stays open.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלָמִים לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה דִּידֵיהּ אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: A peace offering for the sake of his own thanks offering was needed;
it would enter your mind to say:
since a thanks offering is called a 'peace offering,'
peace offerings are also called 'thanks offering,'

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי שָׁחֵיט לְהוּ לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה לִיכַּשְּׁרוּ;
phrases.english: and when one slaughters them for the sake of a thanks offering, they should be fit;
so it teaches us that they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלָמִים לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה דִּידֵיהּ אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10 and leaves the rejection in Step 9 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A 'necessary case' answer: the chosen example teaches its own new lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a תודה is called a שלמים, a שלמים is also called a תודה, so a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה would be כשרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name only works one way, so a שלמים slaughtered as a תודה is פסולה. This lesson justifies the ברייתא's choice of example, so its wording proves nothing about a friend's תודה.

steps.title: A sin offering for a sin offering is fit, but not for a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת is כשרה, but a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering is fit. If it was slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבא gives a ruling about a חטאת slaughtered with the wrong intent, and this sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the intent stays within the same type of offering, a חטאת for a חטאת, the offering is כשרה. If the intent switches to a different type, a חטאת for an עולה, it is פסולה. This matches the pattern of the earlier תודה discussion: the same type is treated differently from a different type.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering.
A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מִזְבֵּחַ.
Fit. The offering is valid.
Unfit. The offering is invalid.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering is fit,
phrases.notes: He means a different sin offering, like one the owner owes for another sin.

phrases.english: for the sake of a burnt offering, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תודה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת is כשרה. A חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is פסולה.

steps.title: The source for רבא's first ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת is כשרה. It answers from the פסוק "and slaughter it for a חטאת": the animal only has to be slaughtered as a חטאת, any חטאת. Slaughtering it as an עולה is the wrong type, so it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The תורה says, "And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering." Here, a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering, so it is fine. If it was slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבא's ruling from step 12 and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only demands that the animal be slaughtered "for a חטאת", meaning with the right TYPE in mind. Thinking of a different חטאת still matches that requirement, so the animal stays כשרה. Thinking of an עולה is the wrong type, so it fails the requirement and is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? The גמרא is asking for the source of a ruling.
"The Merciful One", a way of referring to the Torah or to ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah.
For the sake of, meaning with the intent that it be a certain type of offering.
A burnt offering, which is completely burned on the מזבח.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering," says the Torah,
and here, a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering.
For the sake of a burnt offering, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״וְשָׁחַט אוֹתָהּ לְחַטָּאת״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבא's ruling in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת is כשרה, but one slaughtered for an עולה is פסולה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק only requires slaughtering "for a חטאת". Any חטאת meets that requirement; an עולה does not.

steps.title: A חטאת slaughtered for a different person
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new ruling about the PERSON the חטאת is slaughtered for. If it is slaughtered for someone else who owes a חטאת, it is פסולה. If it is slaughtered for someone who owes an עולה, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A sin offering that was slaughtered for a person who owes a sin offering is unfit. If it was slaughtered for a person who owes a burnt offering, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves from the TYPE of offering to the PERSON the offering is meant for, and gives a new ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the slaughterer has the right type of offering in mind, but the wrong owner. The surprising part is that the result depends on what that other person owes. Someone who owes a חטאת makes it פסולה; someone who owes only an עולה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: On behalf of whom, meaning which person the offering is meant to help.
Obligated, someone who owes a certain offering.
Fit, valid as an offering.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 12. There, "חטאת for a חטאת" (לְשֵׁם, the TYPE) was כשרה. Here, "for a person who owes a חטאת" (עַל, the PERSON) is פסולה. These are two different kinds of wrong intent with opposite results.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A sin offering that he slaughtered for a person
who owes a sin offering is unfit.
phrases.notes: This means a different person, not the owner, who also happens to owe a חטאת.

phrases.english: For a person who owes a burnt offering, it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ עַל מִי שֶׁמְּחוּיָּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by the same אמורא. It shifts from intent about the type of offering to intent about the person it is for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for another person who owes a חטאת is פסולה. One slaughtered for a person who owes an עולה is כשרה.

steps.title: The source: "atonement for him"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's ruling from "and he shall atone for him". The atonement must be for the owner, not for another person. But the "other person" the פסוק excludes is someone like the owner, who needs the same kind of atonement, meaning a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? "And he shall atone for him": for him, and not for another person. And that other person is one similar to him, someone who needs the same atonement he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind רבא's ruling in step 14 and explains why it only disqualifies a person who owes a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "For him" excludes "another person". The גמרא reads that other person as someone comparable to the owner, who owes the same kind of atonement, a חטאת. A person who owes only an עולה is not "like him", so slaughtering the חטאת for that person does not disqualify it.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall atone for him", from the פסוק about the חטאת.
His fellow, another person who is not the owner.
Similar to him, in the same situation as the owner.
Atonement, forgiveness that comes through the offering.

steps.whatToRemember: "For him and not for another" only excludes another person who is LIKE the owner, someone who also needs a חטאת's atonement.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And he shall atone for him":
for him, and not for his fellow;
his fellow who is similar to him,
in that he owes the same atonement as him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו״ – עָלָיו וְלֹא עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבא's ruling in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why another person who owes a חטאת disqualifies the offering, but one who owes an עולה does not.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "For him and not for his fellow" means a fellow who is like him and needs the same atonement. Only someone who owes a חטאת fits that description.

steps.title: A חטאת slaughtered for someone who owes nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a חטאת slaughtered for a person who owes no offering at all is פסולה. The reason is that every Jew owes atonement for some positive מצוה, so this person also counts as someone who needs atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A sin offering that was slaughtered for a person who owes nothing at all is unfit, because there is no person in Israel who does not owe something for a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds one more case: a חטאת slaughtered for someone who seems to owe nothing. He rules it פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that someone who owes nothing is even less "like the owner" than someone who owes an עולה, so the offering should be כשרה. רבא says no such person really exists, because everyone has failed at some positive מצוה. So this person counts as someone who needs atonement, and the offering is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything at all.
A positive commandment, a מצוה to actively do something.

steps.whatToRemember: Intent about the TYPE: another חטאת is fine, an עולה is not. Intent about the PERSON: someone who owes a חטאת, or seems to owe nothing, makes it פסולה. Someone who owes only an עולה does not.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A sin offering that he slaughtered for a person
who owes nothing at all is unfit,
because there is no person in Israel
who does not owe something for a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: He means everyone has missed some positive מצוה, so nobody is truly free of needing atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ עַל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּיָּיב כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of steps 14-15 to a person who seems to owe no offering at all, and explains why that person still counts as needing atonement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for someone who owes nothing is פסולה, since every Jew owes atonement for some positive מצוה.

steps.title: A חטאת also atones for missed positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a חטאת atones for people who failed to keep a positive מצוה. He proves it with a קל וחומר: if it atones for sins punished by כרת, it surely atones for lighter failures.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A חטאת atones for people who are liable for failing to do a positive מצוה. This is a קל וחומר: it atones for people liable for כרת, so all the more so it atones for people liable for a positive מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states a new rule: a חטאת also covers failures to do a positive מצוה. He backs it up with a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת normally comes for very serious sins, ones that carry כרת. Missing a positive מצוה is much lighter. If the חטאת works for the heavy case, it should surely work for the light case. This also explains Step 16: since a חטאת can cover a positive מצוה, a person who owes nothing still counts as someone a חטאת could atone for.

keyTerms.meaning: atones, brings forgiveness
people liable for failing to do a positive מצוה
a 'how much more so' argument, from a stricter case to a lighter one
people liable for sins punished by כרת (being cut off)

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A sin offering atones for those liable for a positive מצוה
by an a fortiori argument:
it atones for those liable for karet;

phrases.aramaic: עַל חַיָּיבֵי עֲשֵׂה לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?!
phrases.english: for those liable for a positive מצוה, is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: חַטָּאת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל חַיָּיבֵי עֲשֵׂה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the person in Step 16 counts as 'like the owner': a חטאת can atone for positive-מצוה failures, so someone who owes only for an עשה needs a kind of atonement a חטאת provides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת atones for failing to do a positive מצוה, by a קל וחומר from sins punished by כרת.

steps.title: This seems to contradict רבא's ruling about someone who owes an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a חטאת atones for positive מצוות, then positive-מצוה atonement is the same type as a חטאת. But רבא ruled that a חטאת slaughtered for someone who owes an עולה is כשרה, meaning it is a different type.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this saying that a positive מצוה is the same type as a חטאת? But רבא said: a חטאת slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת is פסולה, and for someone who owes an עולה it is כשרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's new statement by pointing to his own earlier ruling from Step 14, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה comes to atone for a positive מצוה. If a חטאת also atones for positive מצוות, then someone who owes an עולה needs the same kind of atonement as the owner. By Step 15's logic, slaughtering for him should make the חטאת פסולה. Yet רבא ruled it is כשרה, which treats the עולה-owner as needing a different type of atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (opens a challenge to what was just said)
of its type, the same kind
but didn't he say? (brings a contradicting statement)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the animal being slaughtered as an עולה. It is about the PERSON it was slaughtered for, as in Steps 14 and 15.

phrases.english: Is this to say that it is of the same type?!
phrases.notes: He means: is a positive מצוה the same kind of atonement as a חטאת?

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
A sin offering that one slaughtered
for someone who is obligated to bring a sin offering is unfit,
but for someone who is obligated to bring a burnt offering, it is fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּבַת מִינַהּ הִיא?! וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 17 by setting it against רבא's own ruling in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in Step 17 that a חטאת atones for positive מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חטאת covers positive מצוות, then an עולה-owner needs the same type of atonement as the חטאת-owner. Under Step 15's rule, slaughtering for him should make the חטאת פסולה. But רבא ruled it כשרה.
